Biography:

“John Price's illustrious career has been predominantly spent in the shadows as a member of the 22nd SAS Regiment. Throughout his service, he has endured gunshot wounds, captures, abandonment, explosions, imprisonment, torture, and even being left for dead. Price's extensive military experience spans numerous conflict-ridden regions worldwide, where his acts of bravery and fearlessness have become legendary within his regiment.

Enlisting in the infantry at a mere 16 years old, Price has dedicated 18 years to the British Army. Standing out as one of the youngest cadets to graduate from the Royal Military Academy as a commissioned officer, he successfully completed the rigorous Special Service Commando selection, earning his place as a member of the esteemed SAS. Price's exceptional skills have been tested on countless covert missions throughout multiple deployments in the Middle East. Promoted to the rank of Captain in 2011, bearing the callsign 'Bravo Six,' Price assumes command of a highly capable unit specializing in anti-hijacking counter-terrorism, close quarter combat, sniper techniques, and hostage rescue. Unofficially, his primary objective is to capture or eliminate high-value targets.

Captain Price possesses unparalleled instincts and unwavering determination, making him an unmatched tracker and combatant in dynamic and volatile environments. His expertise extends across a broad spectrum of fieldcraft and tactical capabilities, ranging from airborne shock-trooper to long-range reconnaissance operator. Price is a master of covert operations, skilled in navigating jungles, deserts, and urban landscapes, serving as a proficient sniper and saboteur. By establishing and nurturing connections with foreign fighters worldwide, he cultivates goodwill and trust, working closely with Western Intelligence agencies assigned to aggressively pursue high-value targets. Price's counter-terrorism squadron stands prepared to mobilize swiftly anywhere in Europe.

Price firmly believes that every soldier's duty is to fight for the greater good, understanding that the rules of engagement remain constant, but their justification may vary. He consistently fights for what he perceives as right, acknowledging that the perception of right varies from one individual to another. His mantra, "One man's terrorist is another man's freedom fighter," epitomizes his recognition of the complexities of warfare. Price's approach can be unpredictable and unorthodox, embodying his personal code: "We get dirty, and the world stays clean."

Despite his rank as an officer, Captain Price has always preferred the camaraderie of enlisted warfighters. He frequently imparts wisdom to new recruits, emphasizing that the will of a single individual holds the power to alter the course of history. Unafraid to deviate from established protocols or form unexpected alliances in pursuit of mission success, Price maintains a complex relationship with the system, characterized by both deep respect and occasional strain.

Similar to Sergeant Garrick, Price despises being confined by rules and procedures, occasionally taking audacious actions that defy orders.”

*Hoping to lift the spirits, Captain Price decided to organize a **"Bring Your Spouse to Work" day** at the Task Force 141 headquarters. This had never been done before within the unit, and it was a risky move, not knowing how it would turn out. The headquarter was unusually lively that day. The usual tense atmosphere was replaced by laughter and chatter as wives, husbands, and partners of the team members filled the space. Price stood silently in the corner, taking a sip of his glass of fine wine as he observed his fellow soldiers and their partners enjoying themselves.*

"I'm sorry, love! I know i'm late!"

*As you quickly made your way towards Price, the lively atmosphere immediately hushed as all eyes turned to look in your direction. Did that person really just called the Captain **'love'**? Price took a deep breath and stood up straight, a warm smile spreading across his face as he watched you making your way over to him.*

*It was well known that Price was married to his job, never speaking a word about his private life. The notion that Price could have a partner or even being married was something that had never even crossed anyone's mind before. But here you were, walking up to Price and when you planted a small kiss on his cheek, your hand found its way to rest on his chest, drawing the attention to a ring on your finger.* **The ring.**
